passages.text: Then the Israelites traveled on and camped in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
They traveled onward.
They camped in the plains of Moab.
These plains were near the Jordan River.
The camp was across from Jericho.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מֵעֵ֖בֶר לְיַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Now Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites, and Moab was terrified of the people because they were numerous. Indeed, Moab dreaded the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the son of Zippor.
Balak saw everything Israel did to the Amorites.
The people of Israel defeated the Amorites.
Moab was very afraid of the Israelites.
The Israelites were many in number.
Moab dreaded the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥רְא בָּלָ֖ק בֶּן־ צִפּ֑וֹר אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לָֽאֱמֹרִֽי׃ וַיָּ֨גָר מוֹאָ֜ב מִפְּנֵ֥י הָעָ֛ם מְאֹ֖ד כִּ֣י רַב־ ה֑וּא וַיָּ֣קָץ מוֹאָ֔ב מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So the Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “This horde will devour everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” Since Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time, he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people. “Behold, a people has come out of Egypt,” said Balak. “They cover the face of the land and have settled next to me.
passages.sermon:
The Moabites spoke to the elders of Midian.
They said, “This crowd will destroy everything around us.
They will do it like an ox eats the grass of the field.”
At that time, Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab.
Balak sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor.
Balaam lived at Pethor, near the Euphrates River, in the land of his people.
Balak said, “Look, a people has come out of Egypt.
They cover the face of the land.
They have settled next to me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מוֹאָ֜ב אֶל־ זִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן עַתָּ֞ה יְלַחֲכ֤וּ הַקָּהָל֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ סְבִ֣יבֹתֵ֔ינוּ כִּלְחֹ֣ךְ הַשּׁ֔וֹר אֵ֖ת יֶ֣רֶק הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּבָלָ֧ק בֶּן־ צִפּ֛וֹר מֶ֥לֶךְ לְמוֹאָ֖ב בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽוא׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכִ֜ים אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ בְּע֗וֹר פְּ֠תוֹרָה אֲשֶׁ֧ר עַל־ הַנָּהָ֛ר אֶ֥רֶץ בְּנֵי־ עַמּ֖וֹ לִקְרֹא־ ל֑וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִ֠נֵּה עַ֣ם יָצָ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ הִנֵּ֤ה כִסָּה֙ אֶת־ עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְה֥וּא יֹשֵׁ֖ב מִמֻּלִֽי׃

passages.text: So please come now and put a curse on this people, because they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I may be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land; for I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, “Come now.
Curse this people for me.
This people is too strong for me.
Maybe I can defeat them.
Maybe I can drive them out of the land.
I know something about you.
When you bless people, they are blessed.
When you curse people, they are cursed.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֩ לְכָה־ נָּ֨א אָֽרָה־ לִּ֜י אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה כִּֽי־ עָצ֥וּם הוּא֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי אוּלַ֤י אוּכַל֙ נַכֶּה־ בּ֔וֹ וַאֲגָרְשֶׁ֖נּוּ מִן־ הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־ תְּבָרֵךְ֙ מְבֹרָ֔ךְ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּאֹ֖ר יוּאָֽר׃

passages.text: The elders of Moab and Midian departed with the fees for divination in hand. They came to Balaam and relayed to him the words of Balak.
passages.sermon:
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian left their land.
They carried fees for divination in their hands.
They traveled to Balaam.
They spoke to Balaam.
They told Balaam the message from Balak.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ זִקְנֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ וְזִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֔ן וּקְסָמִ֖ים בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו דִּבְרֵ֥י בָלָֽק׃

passages.text: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and I will give you the answer that the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
The princes of Moab came to Balaam.
Balaam spoke to the princes of Moab.
Balaam said, “Stay here tonight.”
Balaam said, “I will tell you what the LORD says to me.”
The princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לִ֤ינוּ פֹה֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ שָׂרֵֽי־ מוֹאָ֖ב עִם־ בִּלְעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”
passages.sermon:
God came to Balaam.
God spoke to Balaam.
God asked Balaam a question.
God said, “Who are these men with you?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֛י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: And Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message: ‘Behold, a people has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I may be able to fight against them and drive them away.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
God spoke to Balaam.
Balaam answered God.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak was the son of Zippor.
Balak sent a message to Balaam.
Balak said, “A people has come out of Egypt.”
These people cover the face of the land.
Balak said, “Come and curse them for me.”
Balak said, “Maybe I can fight them.”
Balak said, “Maybe I can drive them away.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר בִּלְעָ֖ם אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּלָ֧ק בֶּן־ צִפֹּ֛ר מֶ֥לֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב שָׁלַ֥ח אֵלָֽי׃ הִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣א מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וַיְכַ֖ס אֶת־ עֵ֣ין הָאָ֑רֶץ עַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֤ה קָֽבָה־ לִּי֙ אֹת֔וֹ אוּלַ֥י אוּכַ֛ל לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּ֖וֹ וְגֵרַשְׁתִּֽיו׃

passages.text: But God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. You are not to curse this people, for they are blessed.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Balaam.
God said, “Do not go with these men.
Do not curse these people.
These people are blessed.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם לֹ֥א תֵלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּהֶ֑ם לֹ֤א תָאֹר֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בָר֖וּךְ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: So Balaam got up the next morning and said to Balak’s princes, “Go back to your homeland, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
He got up in the morning.
He spoke to the princes of Balak.
He said, “Go back to your homeland.
The LORD has refused to let me go with you.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קָם בִּלְעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ שָׂרֵ֣י בָלָ֔ק לְכ֖וּ אֶֽל־ אַרְצְכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י מֵאֵ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה לְתִתִּ֖י לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And the princes of Moab arose, returned to Balak, and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
passages.sermon:
The princes of Moab stood up.
They returned to Balak.
They spoke to Balak.
They said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
passages.original: וַיָּק֙וּמוּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־ בָּלָ֑ק וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵאֵ֥ן בִּלְעָ֖ם הֲלֹ֥ךְ עִמָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Then Balak sent other princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the first messengers.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak wanted Balaam to come to him.
Balak sent messengers to Balaam before.
Balak sent more princes again.
These princes were more numerous than the first group.
These princes were more important than the first group.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥סֶף ע֖וֹד בָּלָ֑ק שְׁלֹ֣חַ שָׂרִ֔ים רַבִּ֥ים וְנִכְבָּדִ֖ים מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: They came to Balaam and said, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me, for I will honor you richly and do whatever you say. So please come and put a curse on this people for me!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak sent messengers to Balaam.
The messengers came to Balaam.
They spoke to Balaam.
They said, “Balak son of Zippor has a message.”
They said, “Do not let anything stop you from coming to Balak.”
They said, “Balak will honor you greatly.”
They said, “Balak will do whatever you ask him to do.”
They said, “Please come.”
They said, “Curse these people for Balak.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ בָּלָ֣ק בֶּן־ צִפּ֔וֹר אַל־ נָ֥א תִמָּנַ֖ע מֵהֲלֹ֥ךְ אֵלָֽי׃ כִּֽי־ כַבֵּ֤ד אֲכַבֶּדְךָ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֑ה וּלְכָה־ נָּא֙ קָֽבָה־ לִּ֔י אֵ֖ת הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: But Balaam replied to the servants of Balak, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything small or great to go beyond the command of the LORD my God.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak sent his servants to Balaam.
Balaam answered the servants of Balak.
Balaam said, "Even if Balak gave me his whole house filled with silver and gold, I could not do anything against the command of the LORD my God.
I cannot do anything small or great beyond what the LORD says."
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַן בִּלְעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ עַבְדֵ֣י בָלָ֔ק אִם־ יִתֶּן־ לִ֥י בָלָ֛ק מְלֹ֥א בֵית֖וֹ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב לֹ֣א אוּכַ֗ל לַעֲבֹר֙ אֶת־ פִּי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת קְטַנָּ֖ה א֥וֹ גְדוֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: So now, please stay here overnight as the others did, that I may find out what else the LORD has to tell me.”
passages.sermon: Balaam spoke to the servants of Balak.\r\nHe said, "Stay here tonight, just as the others did."\r\nI will find out what more the LORD will say to me.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁב֨וּ נָ֥א בָזֶ֛ה גַּם־ אַתֶּ֖ם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְאֵ֣דְעָ֔ה מַה־ יֹּסֵ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה דַּבֵּ֥ר עִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: That night God came to Balaam and said, “Since these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them, but you must only do what I tell you.”
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
Balaam is a man whom God spoke to.
That night, God came to Balaam.
God spoke to Balaam.
God said, “These men have come to call you.
Get up.
Go with them.
But you must do only what I tell you.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀ אֶל־ בִּלְעָם֮ לַיְלָה֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אִם־ לִקְרֹ֤א לְךָ֙ בָּ֣אוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים ק֖וּם לֵ֣ךְ אִתָּ֑ם וְאַ֗ךְ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־ אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֹת֥וֹ תַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: So in the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
He got up in the morning.
He saddled his donkey.
He went with the princes of Moab.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קָם בִּלְעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַֽיַּחֲבֹ֖שׁ אֶת־ אֲתֹנ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ עִם־ שָׂרֵ֥י מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: Then God’s anger was kindled because Balaam was going along, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
passages.sermon:
God became angry.
Balaam was going along the road.
The angel of the LORD stood in the road.
The angel opposed Balaam.
Balaam rode his donkey.
Two servants went with Balaam.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֣ף אֱלֹהִים֮ כִּֽי־ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הוּא֒ וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֞ב מַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ לְשָׂטָ֣ן ל֑וֹ וְהוּא֙ רֹכֵ֣ב עַל־ אֲתֹנ֔וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י נְעָרָ֖יו עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the path and went into a field. So Balaam beat her to return her to the path.
passages.sermon:
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD.
The angel stood in the road.
The angel held a sword in his hand.
The sword was drawn.
The donkey left the road.
The donkey went into a field.
Balaam beat the donkey.
Balaam wanted the donkey to return to the road.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָאָתוֹן֩ אֶת־ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה נִצָּ֣ב בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ וְחַרְבּ֤וֹ שְׁלוּפָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וַתֵּ֤ט הָֽאָתוֹן֙ מִן־ הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ בִּלְעָם֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אָת֔וֹן לְהַטֹּתָ֖הּ הַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow passage between two vineyards, with walls on either side.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD stood in the path.
This path was narrow.
There were vineyards on both sides of the path.
There was a wall on one side.
There was a wall on the other side.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה בְּמִשְׁע֖וֹל הַכְּרָמִ֑ים גָּדֵ֥ר מִזֶּ֖ה וְגָדֵ֥ר מִזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And the donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against it. So he beat her once again.
passages.sermon:
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD.
The angel of the LORD stood nearby.
The donkey pressed herself against the wall.
She crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall.
Balaam beat the donkey again.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֨רֶא הָאָת֜וֹן אֶת־ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַתִּלָּחֵץ֙ אֶל־ הַקִּ֔יר וַתִּלְחַ֛ץ אֶת־ רֶ֥גֶל בִּלְעָ֖ם אֶל־ הַקִּ֑יר וַיֹּ֖סֶף לְהַכֹּתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn to the right or left.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD appeared.
The angel of the LORD moved forward.
He stood in a very narrow place.
There was no room to turn to the right.
There was no room to turn to the left.
passages.original: וַיּ֥וֹסֶף מַלְאַךְ־ יְהוָ֖ה עֲב֑וֹר וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם צָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵֽין־ דֶּ֥רֶךְ לִנְט֖וֹת יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול׃

passages.text: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam, and he became furious and beat her with his staff.
passages.sermon:
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD.
The donkey lay down under Balaam.
Balaam became very angry.
Balaam beat the donkey with his staff.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֤רֶא הָֽאָתוֹן֙ אֶת־ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּרְבַּ֖ץ תַּ֣חַת בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֣ף בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הָאָת֖וֹן בַּמַּקֵּֽל׃

passages.text: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave the donkey the ability to speak.
The donkey spoke to Balaam.
The donkey asked Balaam a question.
The donkey said, “What have I done to you?”
The donkey said, “Why have you beaten me these three times?”
passages.original: וַיִּפְתַּ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ פִּ֣י הָאָת֑וֹן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לְבִלְעָם֙ מֶה־ עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי לְךָ֔ כִּ֣י הִכִּיתַ֔נִי זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ רְגָלִֽים׃

passages.text: Balaam answered the donkey, “You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now!”
passages.sermon: Balaam spoke to the donkey.\r\nHe said, “You have made a fool of me.”\r\nHe said, “If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ לָֽאָת֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִתְעַלַּ֖לְתְּ בִּ֑י ל֤וּ יֶשׁ־ חֶ֙רֶב֙ בְּיָדִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה הֲרַגְתִּֽיךְ׃

passages.text: But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not the donkey you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” “No,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
The donkey spoke to Balaam.
The donkey said, “I am your donkey.
You have ridden me all your life until today.
Have I ever acted this way toward you before?”
Balaam answered, “No.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָאָת֜וֹן אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֗ם הֲלוֹא֩ אָנֹכִ֨י אֲתֹֽנְךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר־ רָכַ֣בְתָּ עָלַ֗י מֵעֽוֹדְךָ֙ עַד־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הַֽהַסְכֵּ֣ן הִסְכַּ֔נְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְךָ֖ כֹּ֑ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹֽא׃

passages.text: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted.
The LORD opened Balaam’s eyes.
Balaam was a prophet.
Balaam saw the angel of the LORD.
The angel stood in the road.
The angel held a sword.
The sword was drawn in the angel’s hand.
Balaam bowed down.
Balaam fell facedown.
passages.original: וַיְגַ֣ל יְהוָה֮ אֶת־ עֵינֵ֣י בִלְעָם֒ וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־ מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ נִצָּ֣ב בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלֻפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיִּקֹּ֥ד וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לְאַפָּֽיו׃

passages.text: The angel of the LORD asked him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Balaam.
The angel asked Balaam a question.
The angel said, “Why did you beat your donkey three times?”
The angel continued speaking.
The angel said, “I have come out to oppose you.”
The angel explained the reason.
The angel said, “Your way is perverse before me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה עַל־ מָ֗ה הִכִּ֙יתָ֙ אֶת־ אֲתֹ֣נְךָ֔ זֶ֖ה שָׁל֣וֹשׁ רְגָלִ֑ים הִנֵּ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ יָצָ֣אתִי לְשָׂטָ֔ן כִּֽי־ יָרַ֥ט הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ לְנֶגְדִּֽי׃

passages.text: The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, then by now I would surely have killed you and let her live.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Balaam.
The angel said, "The donkey saw me."
The donkey turned away from me three times.
If the donkey had not turned away from me,
I would have killed you by now.
I would have let the donkey live."
passages.original: וַתִּרְאַ֙נִי֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֵּ֣ט לְפָנַ֔י זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֑ים אוּלַי֙ נָטְתָ֣ה מִפָּנַ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֛ה גַּם־ אֹתְכָ֥ה הָרַ֖גְתִּי וְאוֹתָ֥הּ הֶחֱיֵֽיתִי׃

passages.text: “I have sinned,” Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me. And now, if this is displeasing in your sight, I will go back home.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam spoke to the angel of the LORD.
Balaam said, “I have sinned.”
Balaam did not know the angel was standing in the road to confront him.
Balaam said, “If this is evil in your eyes, I will return home.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם אֶל־ מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ חָטָ֔אתִי כִּ֚י לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה נִצָּ֥ב לִקְרָאתִ֖י בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְעַתָּ֛ה אִם־ רַ֥ע בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ אָשׁ֥וּבָה לִּֽי׃

passages.text: But the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you are to speak only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Balaam.
The angel said, “Go with these men.”
The angel commanded Balaam to speak only the words God would give him.
Balaam obeyed the angel.
Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֗ם לֵ֚ךְ עִם־ הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶ֗פֶס אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־ אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֹת֣וֹ תְדַבֵּ֑ר וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בִּלְעָ֖ם עִם־ שָׂרֵ֥י בָלָֽק׃

passages.text: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak heard news about Balaam.
Balak learned that Balaam was coming.
Balak decided to go out and meet Balaam.
Balak went to a city in Moab.
This city was on the border of the Arnon River.
The city was at the edge of Balak’s territory.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע בָּלָ֖ק כִּ֣י בָ֣א בִלְעָ֑ם וַיֵּצֵ֨א לִקְרָאת֜וֹ אֶל־ עִ֣יר מוֹאָ֗ב אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ גְּב֣וּל אַרְנֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַגְּבֽוּל׃

passages.text: And he said to Balaam, “Did I not send you an urgent summons? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to richly reward you?”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, “I sent messengers to call you.”
“I sent them urgently.”
“Why did you not come to me?”
“Do you think I am not able to honor you?”
“Do you think I cannot give you a great reward?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בָּלָ֜ק אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֗ם הֲלֹא֩ שָׁלֹ֨חַ שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לִקְרֹא־ לָ֔ךְ לָ֥מָּה לֹא־ הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֵלָ֑י הַֽאֻמְנָ֔ם לֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל כַּבְּדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “See, I have come to you,” Balaam replied, “but can I say just anything? I must speak only the word that God puts in my mouth.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam spoke to Balak.
Balaam said, “I have come to you now.
But I cannot say whatever I want.
I must speak only what God puts in my mouth.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם אֶל־ בָּלָ֗ק הִֽנֵּה־ בָ֙אתִי֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ עַתָּ֕ה הֲיָכ֥וֹל אוּכַ֖ל דַּבֵּ֣ר מְא֑וּמָה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׂ֧ים אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּפִ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: So Balaam accompanied Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from another nation.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak wanted Balaam to come to him.
Balaam went with Balak.
They traveled together.
They arrived at Kiriath-huzoth.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בִּלְעָ֖ם עִם־ בָּלָ֑ק וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ קִרְיַ֥ת חֻצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and he gave portions to Balaam and the princes who were with him.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak sacrificed cattle.
Balak sacrificed sheep.
Balak gave portions of the meat to Balaam.
Balak gave portions of the meat to the princes who were with Balaam.
passages.original: וַיִּזְבַּ֥ח בָּלָ֖ק בָּקָ֣ר וָצֹ֑אן וַיְשַׁלַּ֣ח לְבִלְעָ֔ם וְלַשָּׂרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The next morning, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the outskirts of the camp of the people.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam was a prophet from another land.
In the morning, Balak took Balaam with him.
Balak led Balaam up to a place called Bamoth-baal.
From Bamoth-baal, Balaam looked out.
Balaam saw the edge of the Israelite camp from there.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח בָּלָק֙ אֶת־ בִּלְעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲלֵ֖הוּ בָּמ֣וֹת בָּ֑עַל וַיַּ֥רְא מִשָּׁ֖ם קְצֵ֥ה הָעָֽם׃
